video.title: Watch This Overlooked AI Tool Build Me a Business in 23 Minutes

summary: Chris Koerner demonstrates finding, validating and launching a business idea in one sitting using Replit Agent 3. He uses Google Trends and Google autocomplete to spot demand for free invoicing software for contractors, then vibe-codes an AI chat/email invoicing app with Stripe payment links and Resend email, and publishes it on a new domain (invoicefree.com). The app works after fixing email-domain verification, though emails land in spam. Key takeaway: search trends plus autocomplete are a cheap demand signal, and AI app builders can produce a working MVP in under an hour; Koerner says he does not plan to turn it into a business.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; builds the app live with Replit Agent 3

ideas.name: Invoice Freely: AI chat/email invoicing for contractors
ideas.one_liner: Free natural-language invoicing app where contractors text, email or chat a request and the customer gets an invoice with a Stripe payment link; revenue from a markup on card processing.
ideas.business_model: Free software monetised by a markup on Stripe card processing (about 0.5% on top of Stripe's 2.9%).
ideas.customer: Small businesses and contractors (tree trimmers, roofers, general contractors, home service businesses, gutter cleaners) who dislike filling in CRM/invoicing forms.
ideas.problem: Invoicing software is painful and rarely industry-specific; contractors on a job site do not want to log into a CRM and fill in name, phone, email and address.
ideas.offer: Free invoicing software where the user types or emails something like 'send an invoice for $800 to Mary Smith for tree trimming services'; the app extracts the details with OpenAI, asks for confirmation, and emails the customer an invoice with a Stripe checkout link. Includes a dashboard of invoices sent, paid and pending.

pricing.model: Free to users; platform earns a processing markup (e.g. about 3.5% charged vs Stripe's ~2.9%); users can mark it up or pass it on
pricing.notes: The transcript garbles the figure ('3 12%'), most likely '3 1/2%' (3.5%). He calls the margin 'half a percent', though 3.5% minus 2.9% is about 0.6%. Not a stated price to customers.

acquisition_channels.details: Host plans a lead capture / email capture / lead magnet on the site and exposure from this video; no real acquisition plan stated.

quote.text: I better get some sort of a lead capture, email capture, lead magnet on this because once this video goes live
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: The YouTube audience is expected to try the app after the video goes live.

ideas.delivery: Software delivered as a web app on a custom domain, built with Replit Agent 3. Uses OpenAI API for natural language parsing, Stripe for payment links and Resend for transactional email. Text/SMS via Twilio was left out of the MVP because of US A2P registration (about 2 weeks).
unit_economics_claims: Even 100 customers could be $1,000/month with almost no cost (hypothetical)
Over 33 million small businesses need invoicing software
ideas.startup_cost: About $11 for the domain plus Replit subscription and API usage (not stated); Resend free plan expected to suffice.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: not stated; a working MVP was built in under an hour, but no revenue and no stated plan to run it as a business

acquisition.how: No acquisition plan exists yet. Inbound routes (SEO, directories, app listings, ads) could be run by agents; cold outreach to sole traders would be restricted in the UK under PECR.

onboarding.how: Self-serve signup and chat interface; an agent can handle setup, with occasional human review.

delivery.how: The product is software: OpenAI parses the request, Stripe and Resend handle payment and email. Deliverability issues (spam folder) need occasional fixes.

billing.how: Stripe processes payments and the platform markup is automatic; the host would handle payouts, tax and Stripe Connect setup.

support.how: AI support agents can field most questions, but payment disputes and failed emails need human escalation.

uk_applicability.notes: Software idea works in the UK with changes: Stripe supported, UK contractors and sole traders need invoices and VAT handling (Making Tax Digital), and a 0.5% markup needs Stripe Connect/payments compliance. A2P registration is US-specific; UK SMS is simpler. Market is very crowded (Xero, FreeAgent, QuickBooks, Zoho).

risks: Invoice emails from a no-reply address landed in spam
Payments markup may need Stripe Connect and regulatory compliance
Early AI-generated app had bugs (wrong $150 amount, emails not arriving)
Free pricing means revenue depends on payment volume
Host himself says he does not plan to run it as a business

tactics.name: Google Trends + autocomplete niche discovery
steps: Search a broad product keyword in Google Trends and set the range to 5 years to confirm it is rising
Type the keyword plus a space into google.com and read the autocomplete suffixes as demand signals
Note unexpected terms (e.g. 'free') that show what buyers want
Pick a suffix that maps to a big niche (e.g. contractors) and rewrite the product idea for it

quote.text: I'm going to go to google.com just to the homepage and type in invoicing software 4.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Monetise a free tool through payment processing markup
steps: Offer the software free
Process payments through Stripe at about 2.9%
Charge a slightly higher rate (about 3.5%) and keep the difference of roughly half a percent
Let customers pass the fee on or mark it up to their clients

tactics.name: Vibe-code an MVP with Replit Agent 3
steps: Write one clear prompt describing the product and the simplest functional version
Prepare API keys first (Stripe secret key starting SK, Stripe public key starting PK, Resend, OpenAI)
Store keys in Replit Secrets
Ask the agent to verify the keys work
Test in preview, then paste errors and observations back to the agent
Publish to the Replit domain first, then connect the custom domain via DNS records

quote.text: Let's oneshot prompt this bad boy.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Set up Resend with a spare domain for transactional email
steps: Add a domain you own in Resend
Add the MX, TXT (SPF/DKIM) and DMARC records at your registrar's advanced DNS
Wait for verification
Set a FROM_EMAIL secret such as no-reply@verified-domain
Use a different domain from the app domain if desired, since it only sends and does not receive

tactics.name: Launch an ugly MVP
steps: Start with the simplest working version (scooter, not car)
Defer things like A2P registration, logo, perfect design and business plan
Launch, then upgrade over time

quote.text: if you're not at least a little bit embarrassed by version one of your product or service, then you probably waited too long to launch.

lessons.lesson: A crowded market can still be worth entering if it is large and customers are unhappy; a vertical focus gives a way to stand out.

lessons.lesson: 'Free' demand can be monetised indirectly, for example by taking a small cut of payment flow.
Ship an ugly MVP quickly instead of polishing; friction before launch kills projects.

quote.text: we're in the business of launching fast, moving fast and breaking things.

lessons.lesson: Choose a name that is broad, easy to spell and says what you do so it does not box you into a sub-niche.
AI app builders now handle full-stack MVPs with payments and email, but integration plumbing (DNS, email auth, spam) still needs human debugging.
Feeding observations from third-party dashboards (e.g. Resend queue status) back to the AI agent speeds up debugging.
Keep the human confirmation step on money-related AI actions such as sending invoices.

quote.text: I kind of like confirming it.

evidence_quality.rationale: This is a live product demo rather than a validated business. The host says he does not plan to run the app as a business, there is no customer, revenue or conversion data, and the economics are hypothetical. The tool demo itself is first-hand and credible, but the market 'validation' is only search-trend evidence.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes his TK Owners community and Replit (says it is not an ad, but it is a product showcase); asks viewers to subscribe.

extraction.review_notes: The extraction is accurate and well grounded. It captures the free invoicing app, the processing-markup model, and the host's statement that he will not run it as a business. Evidence rating C and the promotional conflict (TK Owners, Replit showcase) are appropriate. The only real error is reading the garbled '3 12%' as 3.4%; it most likely means 3.5%. Treating the Trends-plus-autocomplete method as idea I2 is a stylistic choice and was left as is.
